title.zh: 卷七十一 列傳第三十一 徐湛 江湛 王僧綽
title.en: Volume 71 Biographies 31: Xu Zhan, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchao
title.raw: 卷七十一 列傳第三十一 徐湛 江湛 王僧綽 Volume 71 Biographies 31: Xu Zhan, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchao

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十一 徐湛之江湛王僧綽

translations.literal: Biography 31: Xu Zhanzhi, Jiang Zhan, Wang Sengchuo
translations.idiomatic: Biography 31: Xu Zhanzhi, Jiang Zhan, and Wang Sengchuo

sentences.zh: 徐湛之，字孝源，東海郯人。

translations.literal: Xu Zhanzhi, styled Xiaoyuan, was a man of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhanzhi, styled Xiaoyuan, came from Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 司徒羨之兄孫，吳郡太守佩之弟子也。

translations.literal: He was the grandson of the elder brother of Grand Tutor Xianzhi, and a nephew of Wu commandery Administrator Peizhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was a grandson of Grand Tutor Xianzhi's elder brother and a nephew of Wu commandery Administrator Peizhi.

sentences.zh: 祖欽之，秘書監。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qinzh was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qinzh had served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父逵之，尚高祖長女會稽公主，為振威將軍、彭城、沛二郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Kuizhi married Emperor Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Kuaiji, and served as General Who Quells Might and as administrator of both Pengcheng and Pei commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuizhi married Emperor Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Kuaiji, and held the posts of General Who Quells Might and administrator of Pengcheng and Pei commanderies.

sentences.zh: 高祖諸子並幼，以逵之姻戚，將大任之，欲先令立功。

translations.literal: As all of Gaozu's sons were still young, and because Kuizhi was a relative by marriage, Gaozu intended to place great trust in him and wished him first to win merit in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's sons were all still young; because Kuizhi was a kinsman by marriage, Gaozu meant to entrust him with great responsibility and wanted him to earn merit in battle first.

sentences.zh: 及討司馬休之，使統軍為前鋒，配以精兵利器，事克，當即授荊州。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Sima Xiuzhi, he made Kuizhi commander of the vanguard army, equipped with elite troops and fine weapons; if the affair succeeded, he was to be given Jing province immediately.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi, he put Kuizhi in command of the vanguard with picked troops and sharp weapons; once victory was won, he was to receive Jing province at once.

sentences.zh: 休之遣魯宗之子軌擊破之，於陣見害。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi sent Zongzi Gui of Lu to strike and defeat him; Kuizhi was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi sent Zongzi Gui of Lu to rout him, and Kuizhi was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 追贈中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 湛之幼孤，為高祖所愛，常與江夏王義恭寢食不離於側。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi was orphaned young and beloved by Gaozu; he often ate and slept at the side of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, never leaving him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi lost his father young and was cherished by Gaozu; he often ate and slept beside Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and rarely left his side.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，詔曰：「永興公主一門嫡長，早罹辛苦。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu, an edict stated: "Princess Yongxing, as the eldest legitimate daughter of her house, suffered hardship early.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu an edict said: "Princess Yongxing, the eldest legitimate daughter of her line, suffered hardship early in life.

sentences.zh: 外孫湛之，特所鍾愛。

translations.literal: Her grandson Zhanzhi is especially cherished.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandson Zhanzhi is especially beloved.

sentences.zh: 且致節之胤，情實兼常。

translations.literal: Moreover, as a scion who upholds integrity, his feelings are genuinely beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as a descendant who upholds integrity, his disposition is truly out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 可封枝江縣侯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He may be enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhijiang county, with a fief of five hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhijiang county with a fief of five hundred households."

sentences.zh: 」年數歲，與弟淳之共車行，牛奔車壞，左右馳來赴之。

translations.literal: When he was only a few years old, he rode in a carriage with his younger brother Chunzhi; the ox bolted and the carriage broke; attendants rushed up to help.
translations.idiomatic: When he was only a few years old he rode in a carriage with his younger brother Chunzhi; the ox bolted, the carriage broke, and attendants rushed to their aid.

sentences.zh: 湛之先令取弟，眾咸歎其幼而有識。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi first ordered them to fetch his brother; all admired his discernment even as a child.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi first told them to rescue his brother; everyone marveled that even as a child he showed such sense.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗涉大義，善自位待。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he steeped himself considerably in moral principle and knew how to comport himself with restraint.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he steeped himself in moral principle and knew how to keep his place with restraint.

sentences.zh: 事祖母及母，並以孝謹聞。

translations.literal: In serving his grandmother and his mother he was alike known for filial care and circumspection.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his grandmother and his mother alike he won renown for filial devotion and circumspection.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，除著作佐郎，員外散騎侍郎，並不就。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Writing Office and supernumerary Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, but accepted neither post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia he was named Assistant Gentleman of the Writing Office and supernumerary Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, but declined both appointments.

sentences.zh: 六年，東宮始建，起家補太子洗馬，轉國子博士，遷奮威將軍、南彭城、沛二郡太守，徙黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the Eastern Palace was first established, he entered service as Senior Libationer to the Heir Apparent, became Erudite of the National University, was promoted to General Who Exerts Might and administrator of Nan Pengcheng and Pei commanderies, and transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the Eastern Palace was first set up, he began service as Senior Libationer to the Heir Apparent, became Erudite of the National University, was promoted to General Who Exerts Might and administrator of Nan Pengcheng and Pei commanderies, and moved to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 祖母年老，辭以朝直，不拜。

translations.literal: His grandmother was old; he declined on the ground of palace duty and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother was elderly; he pleaded palace attendance duties and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 復授二郡，加輔國將軍，遷秘書監，領右軍將軍，轉侍中，加驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was again given the two commanderies, with the additional title General Who Assists the State; he moved to Director of the Secretariat, concurrently served as General of the Right Army, became Palace Attendant, and was further given the title General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was again given the two commanderies with the added title General Who Assists the State, became Director of the Secretariat while serving concurrently as General of the Right Army, was made Palace Attendant, and received the further title General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 復為秘書監，加散騎常侍，驍騎如故。

translations.literal: He again served as Director of the Secretariat, with the added title Regular Attendant Cavalier, retaining his post as General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Director of the Secretariat with the added title Regular Attendant Cavalier, retaining General of Valiant Cavalry as before.

sentences.zh: 會稽公主身居長嫡，為太祖所禮，家事大小，必咨而後行。

translations.literal: Princess Kuaiji, as the eldest legitimate daughter, was honored by Taizu; matters large and small in the household were always referred to her before action.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Kuaiji, as the eldest legitimate daughter, was honored by Taizu; no matter in the household, great or small, was undertaken until she had been consulted.

sentences.zh: 西征謝晦，使公主留止台內，總攝六宮。

translations.literal: When Taizu marched west against Xie Hui, he had the princess remain inside the palace, in overall charge of the six palaces.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign against Xie Hui, he had the princess remain within the palace precincts to oversee the six palaces in general.

sentences.zh: 忽有不得意，輒號哭，上甚憚之。

translations.literal: Whenever something displeased her she would burst into wailing; the emperor greatly feared this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever something displeased her she would break into loud weeping; the emperor was deeply wary of this.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖微時，貧陋過甚，嘗自往新洲伐荻，有納布衫襖等衣，皆敬皇后手自作；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu was still obscure, his poverty had been extreme; he once went himself to Xinzhou to cut reeds, and owned cotton jacket and padded garment and other clothes, all made by Empress Dowager Jing with her own hands;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gaozu was still obscure, his poverty had been extreme; he once went himself to Xinzhou to cut reeds, and had cotton jacket, padded coat, and other garments—all made by Empress Dowager Jing with her own hands;

sentences.zh: 高祖既貴，以此衣付公主，曰：「後世若有驕奢不節者，可以此衣示之。

translations.literal: After Gaozu rose to eminence he entrusted these clothes to the princess, saying, "If in later generations there is one who is arrogant, extravagant, and unrestrained, show them these garments."
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu rose to eminence he gave these garments to the princess, saying, "If later generations produce someone arrogant, extravagant, and unrestrained, you may show them these clothes."

sentences.zh: 」湛之為大將軍彭城王義康所愛，與劉湛等頗相附協。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi won the affection of Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang and rather closely associated with Liu Tan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi won the favor of Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang and associated rather closely with Liu Tan and others.

sentences.zh: 及劉湛得罪，事連湛之，太祖大怒，將致大辟。

translations.literal: When Liu Tan fell from favor, the affair implicated Zhanzhi; Taizu was furious and was about to impose the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Tan fell from favor the affair implicated Zhanzhi as well; Taizu was furious and was about to impose the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 湛之憂懼無計，以告公主。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi, anxious and at a loss, told the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi, anxious and at his wits' end, told the princess.

sentences.zh: 公主即日入宮，既見太祖，因號哭下床，不復施臣妾之禮。

translations.literal: That very day the princess entered the palace; having seen Taizu, she wailed and threw herself from the couch, no longer observing the ceremonies due a subject and wife.
translations.idiomatic: That very day the princess entered the palace; once she had seen Taizu she wailed and threw herself from the couch, no longer observing the ceremonies owed a subject and wife.

sentences.zh: 以錦囊盛高祖納衣，擲地以示上曰：「汝家本貧賤，此是我母為汝父作此納衣。

translations.literal: She packed Gaozu's cotton garments in a brocade pouch and hurled them to the ground to show the emperor, saying, "Your family was originally poor and lowly; this is the cotton garment my mother made for your father."
translations.idiomatic: She packed Gaozu's cotton garments in a brocade pouch and flung them to the ground before the emperor, saying, "Your family was originally poor and lowly—this is the cotton garment my mother made for your father."

sentences.zh: 今日有一頓飽食，便欲殘害我兒子！

translations.literal: Now that you have one full meal to your satisfaction, you would harm my son!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have had your fill for one meal, you would destroy my son!"

sentences.zh: 」上亦號哭，湛之由此得全也。

translations.literal: The emperor wept as well; Zhanzhi was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as well, and Zhanzhi was thereby spared.

sentences.zh: 遷中護軍，未拜，又遷太子詹事，尋加侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Palace Guard, did not accept, was again made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, and soon added as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Palace Guard but did not accept; he was then made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and soon afterward added as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 湛之善於尺牘，音辭流暢。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi excelled at letters; his tones and phrasing flowed with ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi excelled at correspondence; his tone and phrasing flowed with ease.

sentences.zh: 貴戚豪家，產業甚厚。

translations.literal: As a noble kinsman of a great house, his estates were very substantial.
translations.idiomatic: As a noble kinsman of a great house, his estates were very substantial.

sentences.zh: 室宇園池，貴游莫及。

translations.literal: His halls, gardens, and ponds were unmatched among the titled gentry.
translations.idiomatic: His halls, gardens, and ponds were unmatched among the titled gentry.

sentences.zh: 伎樂之妙，冠絕一時。

translations.literal: The excellence of his performers and music was supreme for the age.
translations.idiomatic: The excellence of his performers and music was unmatched in the age.

sentences.zh: 門生千餘人，皆三吳富人之子，姿質端妍，衣服鮮麗。

translations.literal: He had more than a thousand clients, all sons of wealthy families of the three Wu regions, of fine bearing and in bright, fresh clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He had more than a thousand retainers, all sons of wealthy families of the three Wu regions, handsome in bearing and dressed in bright, fresh clothing.

sentences.zh: 每出入行遊，途巷盈滿，泥雨日，悉以後車載之。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out on excursion, the lanes were full; on muddy rainy days he had them all carried in the rear carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went out on excursion the lanes were packed; on muddy rainy days he had them all carried in the rear carriage.

sentences.zh: 太祖嫌其侈縱，每以為言。

translations.literal: Taizu disliked his extravagance and license, and often spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu disliked his extravagance and license and often spoke of it.

sentences.zh: 時安成公何勖，無忌之子也，臨汝公孟靈休，昶之子也，並各奢豪，與湛之共以肴膳、器服、車馬相尚。

translations.literal: At that time Duke of Ancheng He Xu, son of Wuji, and Duke of Linru Meng Lingxiu, son of Chang, were each sumptuous and proud, and with Zhanzhi vied in food, vessels and dress, carriages and horses.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Duke of Ancheng He Xu, son of Wuji, and Duke of Linru Meng Lingxiu, son of Chang, were each sumptuous and proud; with Zhanzhi they vied in food, vessels and dress, carriages and horses.

sentences.zh: 京邑為之語曰：「安成食，臨汝飾。

translations.literal: The capital said of them: "Ancheng for eating, Linru for ornament."
translations.idiomatic: The capital said of them: "Ancheng for eating, Linru for ornament."

sentences.zh: 」湛之二事之美，兼于何、孟。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi's excellence in both matters combined those of He and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi's excellence in both matters surpassed He and Meng together.

sentences.zh: 勖官至侍中，追諡荒公。

translations.literal: Xu rose to Palace Attendant and was posthumously given the derogatory title Duke Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu rose to Palace Attendant and was posthumously given the derogatory title Duke Huang.

sentences.zh: 靈休善彈棋，官至秘書監。

translations.literal: Lingxiu was skilled at pitch-pot; he reached the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxiu was skilled at pitch-pot and rose to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 湛之遷冠軍將軍、丹陽尹，進號征虜將軍，加散騎常侍，以公主憂不拜。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi was transferred to General Who Crowned Champions and Governor of Danyang, advanced in rank to General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and given Regular Attendant Cavalier; because of mourning for the princess he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi was transferred to General Who Crowned Champions and Governor of Danyang, advanced in rank to General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and given Regular Attendant Cavalier; because of mourning for the princess he did not accept office.

sentences.zh: 過葬，復授前職，湛之表啟固辭，又詣廷尉受罪；

translations.literal: After the funeral he was offered his former posts again; Zhanzhi memorialized firmly declining, and also went to the Minister of Justice to submit to punishment;
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral he was offered his former posts again; Zhanzhi memorialized firmly declining and also went to the Minister of Justice to submit to punishment;

sentences.zh: 上詔獄官勿得受，然後就命。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered the prison officials not to accept his surrender, after which he then took office.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered the prison officials not to accept his surrender, and only then did he take office.

sentences.zh: 固辭常侍，許之。

translations.literal: He firmly declined Regular Attendant Cavalier; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined Regular Attendant Cavalier, and this was granted.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，范曄等謀逆，湛之始與之同，後發其事，所陳多不盡，為曄等款辭所連，乃詣廷尉歸罪，上慰遣令還郡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Fan Ye and others plotted rebellion; Zhanzhi had at first gone along with them, then exposed the affair; what he reported was largely incomplete, and he was implicated by Ye's confessions; he therefore went to the Minister of Justice to admit guilt, and the emperor consoled him and sent him back to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Fan Ye and others plotted rebellion; Zhanzhi had at first gone along with them, then exposed the plot; what he reported was largely incomplete, and he was implicated by Ye's confessions; he therefore went to the Minister of Justice to admit guilt, and the emperor consoled him and sent him back to his commandery.

sentences.zh: 湛之上表曰：

translations.literal: Zhanzhi submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 賊臣范曄、孔熙先等，連結謀逆，法靜尼宣分往還，與大將軍臣義康共相脣齒，備于鞠對。

translations.literal: The traitorous ministers Fan Ye, Kong Xixian, and others linked in plotting rebellion; the nun Fajing and Xixian's emissaries traveled back and forth between them, and with Grand General Yikang they were as lip to teeth, all fully shown in the interrogation record.
translations.idiomatic: The traitorous ministers Fan Ye, Kong Xixian, and others conspired in rebellion; the nun Fajing and Xixian's emissaries traveled back and forth, and with Grand General Yikang they were as lip to teeth—all fully set forth in the interrogation record.

sentences.zh: 伏尋仲承祖始達熙先等意，便極言奸狀。

translations.literal: Reflecting on Zhong Chengzu's first conveying of Xixian's intentions, he immediately set forth the full truth of the treachery in the utmost detail.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on how Zhong Chengzu, once he grasped Xixian's intentions, at once set forth the treachery in full detail,

sentences.zh: 而臣兒女近情，不識大體，上聞之初，不務指斥，紙翰所載，尤復漫略者，實以凶計既表，逆事歸露；

translations.literal: but I, because my children are close at hand, did not grasp the larger picture: at the first report I did not press to denounce them; what my letters recorded was especially cursory—truly because once the wicked design was laid bare and the rebellion revealed,
translations.idiomatic: I, because my children are close at hand, did not grasp the larger picture: at the first report I did not press to denounce them, and what my letters recorded was especially cursory—truly because once the wicked design was laid bare and the rebellion revealed,

sentences.zh: 又仰緣聖慈，不欲窮盡，故言勢依違，未敢縷陳。

translations.literal: and again because I relied on your sacred compassion and did not wish to pursue to the end, my words were therefore evasive and I did not dare set out every strand.
translations.idiomatic: and again because I relied on your sacred compassion and did not wish to pursue the matter to the end, my words were evasive and I did not dare set out every strand.

sentences.zh: 情旨無隱，已昭天鑒。

translations.literal: My true intent, hiding nothing, has already been illuminated by Heaven's mirror.
translations.idiomatic: My true intent, hiding nothing, has already been clear to Heaven's mirror.

sentences.zh: 及群凶收禽，各有所列，曄等口辭，多見誣謗；

translations.literal: When the ringleaders were seized, each gave his own account; Ye's oral statements largely slandered me;
translations.idiomatic: When the ringleaders were seized each gave his own account; Ye's oral statements largely slandered me;

sentences.zh: 承祖醜言，紛紜特甚。

translations.literal: Chengzu's vile words were especially voluminous and confused.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu's vile words were especially voluminous and confused.

sentences.zh: 乃雲臣與義康宿有密契，在省之言，期以為定，潛通姦意，報示天文。

translations.literal: They even said I had long shared a secret pact with Yikang, that words exchanged inside the Secretariat were fixed as the appointed time, that I secretly conveyed treasonous intent and reported celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: They even said I had long shared a secret pact with Yikang, that words exchanged inside the Secretariat fixed the appointed time, that I secretly conveyed treasonous intent and reported celestial signs.

sentences.zh: 末雲熙先縣指必同，以誑於曄，或以智勇見稱，或以愚懦為目。

translations.literal: In the end they said Xixian's pointing finger would surely agree, to deceive Ye—or that I was praised as wise and brave, or held up as stupid and craven.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they said Xixian's pointing finger would surely agree, to deceive Ye—or that I was praised as wise and brave, or held up as stupid and craven.

sentences.zh: 既美其信懷可履，復駭其動止必啟。

translations.literal: They would extol my faith and disposition as reliable, then again alarm themselves that my movements must betray the plot.
translations.idiomatic: They would extol my faith and disposition as reliable, then again alarm themselves that my movements must betray the plot.

sentences.zh: 凡諸詭妄，還自違伐，多舉事端，不究源統，齎傳之信，無有主名，所征之人，又已死沒，首尾乖互，自為矛楯。

translations.literal: All such calumny contradicts itself: it raises many incidents but does not trace them to their source; the credentials it cites have no principal name; the persons it summons are already dead; head and tail clash and become mutual spears.
translations.idiomatic: All such calumny contradicts itself: it raises many incidents but does not trace them to their source; the credentials it cites have no principal name; the persons it summons are already dead; head and tail clash and become mutual spears.

sentences.zh: 即臣誘引之辭，以為始謀之證，銜臣糾告，並見怨咎，縱肆狂言，必規禍陷。

translations.literal: They take my words of enticement as proof of initial conspiracy, resent my denunciation, and all alike heap blame; they give free rein to mad speech, surely intending ruin.
translations.idiomatic: They take my words of enticement as proof of initial conspiracy, resent my denunciation, and all alike heap blame; they give free rein to mad speech, surely intending ruin.

sentences.zh: 伏自探省，亦復有由。

translations.literal: Reflecting inward on myself, there is likewise cause.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting inward on myself, there is likewise cause.

sentences.zh: 昔義康南出之始，敕臣入相伴慰，晨夕覲對，經逾旬日。

translations.literal: When Yikang was first sent south into exile, I was ordered to accompany him in consolation; morning and evening we met face to face for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang was first sent south into exile, I was ordered to accompany him in consolation; morning and evening we met face to face for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 逆圖成謀，雖無顯然，懟容異意，頗形言旨。

translations.literal: Though the rebellious design was not overt, resentment and a different bearing quite appeared in his words and looks.
translations.idiomatic: Though the rebellious design was not overt, resentment and a different bearing quite appeared in his words and looks.

sentences.zh: 遺臣利刃，期以際會，臣苦相諫譬，深加拒塞。

translations.literal: He gave me a sharp blade, with the expectation we would meet at the decisive moment; I bitterly admonished and urged him, and he deeply refused to listen.
translations.idiomatic: He gave me a sharp blade, expecting we would meet at the decisive moment; I bitterly admonished and urged him, and he deeply refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 以為怨憤所至，不足為慮，便以關啟，懼成虛妄，思量反覆，實經愚心，非為納受，曲相蔽匿。

translations.literal: Thinking this was no more than the depth of personal hatred and not worth heed, I closed the matter; fearing it would prove groundless, I turned it over in my mind—truly a foolish heart, not an acceptance of the plot, still less a deliberate cover on my part.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking this was no more than the depth of personal hatred and not worth heed, I closed the matter; fearing it would prove groundless, I turned it over in my mind—truly a foolish heart, not an acceptance of the plot, still less a deliberate cover on my part.

sentences.zh: 又令申情范曄，釋中間之憾，致懷蕭思話，恨婚意未申，謂此僥倖，亦不宣達。

translations.literal: He also had me convey feelings to Fan Ye to resolve ill will between them, and win over Xiao Sihua—resenting that marriage ties had not been fulfilled—and said such chances should not be passed up; I also did not report these.
translations.idiomatic: He also had me convey feelings to Fan Ye to resolve ill will between them, and win over Xiao Sihua—resenting that marriage ties had not been fulfilled—and said such chances should not be passed up; I also did not report these.

sentences.zh: 陛下敦惜天倫，彰于四海，籓禁優簡，親理咸通；

translations.literal: Your Majesty nurtures and cherishes heavenly kinship, making it manifest throughout the realm; restrictions on the princes are generous and simplified, and personal dealings with kinsmen are all permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty nurtures and cherishes heavenly kinship, making it manifest throughout the realm; restrictions on the princes are generous and simplified, and personal dealings with kinsmen are all permitted;

sentences.zh: 又昔蒙眷顧，不容自絕，音翰信命，時相往來。

translations.literal: Moreover I was once shown favor that I could not break off on my own; letters and entrusted messages were exchanged from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I was once shown favor that I could not break off on my own; letters and entrusted messages were exchanged from time to time.

sentences.zh: 或言少意多，旨深文淺，辭色之間，往往難測。

translations.literal: Sometimes a little was said but much was meant, or the purport was deep but the wording shallow, and between tone and color one could often not be sure.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes a little was said but much was meant, or the purport was deep but the wording shallow, and between tone and color one could often not be sure.

sentences.zh: 臣每懼異聞，皆略而不答。

translations.literal: I always feared questionable words and generally answered briefly or not at all.
translations.idiomatic: I always feared questionable words and generally answered briefly or not at all.

sentences.zh: 惟心無邪悖，故不稍以自嫌。

translations.literal: Only because my heart harbored no wicked rebellion did I not much distrust myself on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Only because my heart harbored no wicked rebellion did I not much distrust myself on that account.

sentences.zh: 慺慺丹實，具如此啟。

translations.literal: My earnest loyal truth is fully set forth in this report.
translations.idiomatic: My earnest loyal truth is fully set forth in this report.

sentences.zh: 至於法靜所傳，及熙先等謀，知實不早，見關之日，便即以聞。

translations.literal: As for Fajing's transmissions and Xixian's plots, I truly did not know early; on the day I was implicated I reported at once.
translations.idiomatic: As for Fajing's transmissions and Xixian's plots, I truly did not know early; on the day I was implicated I reported at once.

sentences.zh: 雖晨光幽燭，曲昭窮款，裁以正義，無所逃刑。

translations.literal: Though dawn light illumines the dark and bends to expose my innermost sincerity, measured by righteous law there is no escaping punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Though dawn light illumines the dark and bends to expose my innermost sincerity, measured by righteous law there is no escaping punishment.

sentences.zh: 束骸北闕，請罪司寇，乾施含宥，未加治考，中旨頻降，制使還往，仰荷恩私，哀惶失守。

translations.literal: I would bind my bones at the northern gate and ask punishment from the Minister of Crime; your gracious pardon has not yet applied correction; repeated imperial orders have sent me back and forth; I bear your private kindness and grieve in bewildered loss of composure.
translations.idiomatic: I would bind my bones at the northern gate and ask punishment from the Minister of Crime; your gracious pardon has not yet applied correction; repeated imperial orders have sent me back and forth; I bear your private kindness and grieve in bewildered loss of composure.

sentences.zh: 臣殃積罪深，丁罹酷罰，久應屏棄，永謝人理。

translations.literal: My calamity and accumulated guilt run deep; I have suddenly suffered harsh punishment and should long since have been cast aside, forever cut off from human fellowship.
translations.idiomatic: My calamity and accumulated guilt run deep; I have suddenly suffered harsh punishment and should long since have been cast aside, forever cut off from human fellowship.

sentences.zh: 況奸謀所染，忠孝頓闕，智防愚淺，暗於禍萌，士類未明其心，群庶謂之同惡，朝野側目，眾議沸騰，專信仇隙之辭，不復稍相申體。

translations.literal: How much more when stained by treasonous conspiracy—loyalty and filial piety suddenly fail; wit guards against foolish shallowness, blind to the sprouting of disaster; gentlemen have not made my heart clear, the multitude call me of one wickedness with them; court and countryside fix their eyes on me, public talk seethes; they trust only words borne of enmity and no longer grant the slightest fair hearing.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when stained by treasonous conspiracy—loyalty and filial piety suddenly fail; wit guards against foolish shallowness, blind to the sprouting of disaster; gentlemen have not made my heart clear, the multitude call me of one wickedness with them; court and countryside fix their eyes on me, public talk seethes; they trust only words borne of enmity and no longer grant the slightest fair hearing.

sentences.zh: 臣雖駑下，情非木石。

translations.literal: Though I am mean and low, I am not wood and stone by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am mean and low, I am not wood and stone by nature.

sentences.zh: 豈不知醜點難嬰，伏劍為易。

translations.literal: Do I not know that disgrace is hard to bear and that falling on my sword would be easier?
translations.idiomatic: Do I not know that disgrace is hard to bear and that falling on my sword would be easier?

sentences.zh: 而靦然視息，忍此餘生，實非苟吝微命，假延漏刻。

translations.literal: Yet I calmly draw breath and endure this remnant of life; truly it is not that I meanly cling to a slight existence or borrow extra moments before the water clock runs dry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I calmly draw breath and endure this remnant of life; truly it is not that I meanly cling to a slight existence or borrow extra moments before the water clock runs dry.

sentences.zh: 誠以負戾灰滅，貽惡方來，貪及視息，少自披訴；

translations.literal: It is sincerely because extinction of my guilt would leave malice for those who come after; greedy for the breath still in me, I venture a little self-revelation;
translations.idiomatic: It is sincerely because extinction of my guilt would leave malice for those who come after; greedy for the breath still in me, I venture a little self-revelation;

sentences.zh: 冀幽誠丹款，儻或昭然，雖復身膏草土，九泉無恨。

translations.literal: hoping my hidden sincerity and loyal candor might perchance be clear, so that though my flesh be greased on meadow soil, the nine springs would hold no regret.
translations.idiomatic: hoping my hidden sincerity and loyal candor might perchance be clear, so that though my flesh be greased on meadow soil, the nine springs would hold no regret.

sentences.zh: 顯居官次，垢穢朝班，厚顏何地，可以自處。

translations.literal: To sit lofty in official rank, a stain defiling the court assembly—where in the world can such a thick face find footing?
translations.idiomatic: To sit lofty in official rank, a stain defiling the court assembly—where in the world can such a thick face find footing?

sentences.zh: 乞蒙隳放，伏待鈇钅質。

translations.literal: I beg to be cast down and dismissed, to lie prostrate awaiting the axe.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be cast down and dismissed, to lie prostrate awaiting the axe.

sentences.zh: 上優詔不許。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict and would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，服闋，轉中書令，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when mourning ended, he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, holding concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when mourning ended, he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, holding concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 出為前軍將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General of the Forward Army and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General of the Forward Army and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 善於為政，威惠並行。

translations.literal: He was skilled in administration; authority and kindness went together.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in administration; authority and kindness went together.

sentences.zh: 廣陵城舊有高樓，湛之更加修整，南望鐘山。

translations.literal: The old city of Guangling had a tall tower, which Zhanzhi further refurbished so that it looked south toward Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: The old city of Guangling had a tall tower, which Zhanzhi further refurbished so that it looked south toward Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 城北有陂澤，水物豐盛。

translations.literal: North of the city were marshes and ponds, rich in aquatic creatures.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city were marshes and ponds, rich in aquatic creatures.

sentences.zh: 湛之更起風亭、月觀，吹台、琴室，果竹繁茂，花藥成行，招集文士，盡遊玩之適，一時之盛也。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi further raised the Wind Pavilion, Moon Terrace, Flute Tower, and Zither Hall; fruit and bamboo grew thick, flowering herbs lined the paths; he gathered literati and exhausted every delight of wandering— a splendor for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi further raised the Wind Pavilion, Moon Terrace, Flute Tower, and Zither Hall; fruit and bamboo grew thick, flowering herbs lined the paths; he gathered literati and exhausted every delight of wandering—a splendor for the age.

sentences.zh: 時有沙門釋惠休，善屬文，辭采綺豔，湛之與之甚厚。

translations.literal: At that time there was the monk Huìxiū, skilled in composition, his diction brilliantly ornate; Zhanzhi was on very close terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was the monk Huìxiū, skilled in composition, his diction brilliantly ornate; Zhanzhi was on very close terms with him.

sentences.zh: 世祖命使還俗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu ordered him returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ordered him returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 本姓湯，位至揚州從事史。

translations.literal: His original surname was Tang; he rose to Clerk of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Tang; he rose to Clerk of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，復入為丹陽尹，領太子詹事，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he again entered the capital as Governor of Danyang, holding concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he returned to the capital as Governor of Danyang and Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，索虜至瓜步，湛之領兵置佐，與皇太子分守石頭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the northern barbarians reached Guabu; Zhanzhi led troops and set up aides, and with the Crown Prince jointly guarded Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the Northern Wei reached Guabu; Zhanzhi led troops and staff officers and, with the Crown Prince, jointly held Shitou.

sentences.zh: 二十八年春，魯爽兄弟率部曲歸順，爽等，魯軌子也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-eighth year Lu Shuang and his brothers led their followers in submission; Shuang and the others were sons of Lu Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-eighth year Lu Shuang and his brothers led their followers in submission; Shuang and his brothers were sons of Lu Gui.

sentences.zh: 湛之以為廟算遠圖，特所獎納，不敢苟申私怨。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi regarded this as the court's far-reaching design and especially commended and accepted it, not daring lightly to voice private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi regarded this as the court's far-reaching strategy and especially commended it, not daring to press a private grudge.

sentences.zh: 乞屏居田里，不許。

translations.literal: He begged to withdraw and live in the countryside; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire to the countryside; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書僕射，領護軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, holding concurrently General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director of the Secretariat while serving concurrently as General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令何尚之以湛之國戚，任遇隆重，欲以朝政推之。

translations.literal: At that time Director He Shangzhi, because Zhanzhi was a kinsman by marriage, treated him with great favor and wished to turn court affairs over to him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Director He Shangzhi, because Zhanzhi was a kinsman by marriage, favored him heavily and wished to hand court affairs over to him.

sentences.zh: 凡諸辭訴，一不料省。

translations.literal: As for all petitions and suits, he did not examine a single one.
translations.idiomatic: He did not examine a single petition or suit.

sentences.zh: 湛之亦以《職官記》及令文，尚書令敷奏出內，事無不總，令缺則僕射總任。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi also cited the Record of Offices and the ordinance texts: the Director of the Secretariat presents memorials from within, and nothing is not under his overall charge; when the directorate is vacant the vice director assumes overall responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi also cited the Record of Offices and ordinance texts: the Director presents memorials from within and oversees everything; when the directorate is vacant the vice director assumes overall responsibility.

sentences.zh: 又以事歸尚之，互相推委。

translations.literal: He again turned affairs back to Shangzhi; each pushed responsibility onto the other.
translations.idiomatic: He again turned affairs back to Shangzhi, and the two pushed responsibility onto each other.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞袁淑並奏免官，詔曰：「令僕治務所寄，不共求體當，而互相推委，糾之是也。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Shu jointly memorialized to dismiss them from office; an edict stated: "The director and vice director are entrusted with governing affairs; they do not jointly seek what is fitting but push responsibility onto each other—censure of this is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Shu jointly memorialized to dismiss them; an edict said: "The director and vice director are entrusted with governing affairs; instead of jointly seeking what is fitting they push responsibility onto each other—censure is correct."

sentences.zh: 然故事殘舛，所以致茲疑執，特無所問，時詳正之。

translations.literal: Yet precedent is fragmentary and confused, which has produced this disputed hold; they are specially not questioned, and the matter is to be clarified in due course."
translations.idiomatic: Yet precedent is fragmentary and confused, which produced this dispute; they are specially not questioned, and the matter is to be clarified in due course."

sentences.zh: 」乃使湛之與尚之並受辭訴。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi and Shangzhi were then both made to receive petitions and suits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi and Shangzhi were then both ordered to receive petitions and suits.

sentences.zh: 尚之雖為令，而朝事悉歸湛之。

translations.literal: Though Shangzhi was director, all court affairs went to Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shangzhi held the directorate, all court affairs went to Zhanzhi.

sentences.zh: 初，劉湛伏誅，殷景仁卒，太祖委任沈演之、庾炳之、范曄等，後又有江湛、何瑀之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Tan was executed, Yin Jingren died, and Taizu entrusted Shen Yanzi, Yu Bingzhi, Fan Ye, and others; later there were also Jiang Zhan and He Yuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Liu Tan was executed and Yin Jingren died, Taizu entrusted Shen Yanzi, Yu Bingzhi, Fan Ye, and others; later Jiang Zhan and He Yuzhi were added.

sentences.zh: 曄誅，炳之免，演之、瑀之並卒，至是江湛為吏部尚書，與湛之並居權要，世謂之江、徐焉。

translations.literal: Ye was executed, Bingzhi dismissed, Yanzi and Yuzhi both died; by then Jiang Zhan was Director of the Ministry of Personnel and with Zhanzhi jointly held crucial power—the age called them Jiang and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: After Ye was executed, Bingzhi dismissed, and Yanzi and Yuzhi both died, Jiang Zhan became Director of the Ministry of Personnel and with Zhanzhi jointly held crucial power—the age called them Jiang and Xu.

sentences.zh: 上每有疾，湛之輒入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor fell ill, Zhanzhi at once entered to attend him with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor fell ill, Zhanzhi at once entered to attend him with medicine.

sentences.zh: 二凶巫蠱事發，上欲廢劭，賜浚死。

translations.literal: When the witchcraft affair of the two villains broke out, the emperor wished to depose Shao and grant Jun death.
translations.idiomatic: When the witchcraft affair of the two villains broke out, the emperor wished to depose Shao and order Jun to die.

sentences.zh: 而世祖不見寵，故累出外蕃，不得停京輦。

translations.literal: But Emperor Xiaowu was not favored and was repeatedly sent out to border principalities, unable to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: But Emperor Xiaowu was not favored and was repeatedly sent to border principalities, unable to remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 南平王鑠、建平王宏並為上所愛，而鑠妃即湛妹，勸上立之。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanping Shuo and Prince of Jianping Hong were both loved by the emperor, and Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's younger sister; she urged the emperor to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Nanping Shuo and Prince of Jianping Hong were both loved by the emperor; Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's younger sister and urged the emperor to name Shuo heir.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，征鑠自壽陽入朝，既至，又失旨，欲立宏，嫌其非次，是以議久不決。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia, Shuo was summoned from Shouyang to court; once he arrived he again lost favor; the emperor wished to establish Hong but disliked his irregular order of succession, and so deliberation long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanjia, Shuo was summoned from Shouyang to court; once he arrived he again lost favor; the emperor wished to name Hong heir but disliked his irregular order of succession, and deliberation dragged on.

sentences.zh: 與湛之屏人共言論，或連日累夕。

translations.literal: With Zhanzhi he discussed matters away from others, sometimes for days on end through the night.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhanzhi he discussed matters in private, sometimes for days on end through the night.

sentences.zh: 每夜常使湛之自秉燭，繞壁檢行，慮有竊聽者。

translations.literal: Each night he often had Zhanzhi himself hold the candle and walk around the walls on inspection, fearing eavesdroppers.
translations.idiomatic: Each night he often had Zhanzhi hold the candle himself and walk the walls on inspection, fearing eavesdroppers.

sentences.zh: 劭入弑之旦，其夕，上與湛之屏人語，至曉猶未滅燭。

translations.literal: On the dawn when Shao entered to regicide, that very evening the emperor talked with Zhanzhi away from others until dawn, the candles still not extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: On the dawn when Shao entered to kill his father, that very evening the emperor talked with Zhanzhi in private until dawn, the candles still burning.

sentences.zh: 湛之驚起趣北戶，未及開，見害。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi started up in alarm and hurried to the north door; before he could open it he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi started up in alarm and hurried to the north door; before he could open it he was killed.

sentences.zh: 時年四十四。

translations.literal: He was forty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-four.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，追贈司空，加散騎常侍，本官如故，諡曰忠烈公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the added title Regular Attendant Cavalier, his former offices unchanged, posthumous title Duke Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he was posthumously made Minister of Works with the added title Regular Attendant Cavalier, his former offices unchanged, and given the posthumous title Duke Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「徐湛之、江湛、王僧綽門戶荼酷，遺孤流寓，言念既往，感痛兼深。

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "The households of Xu Zhanzhi, Jiang Zhan, and Wang Sengchuo have suffered bitter ruin; their orphaned survivors wander abroad; speaking of the past, grief and pain are alike deep."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "The households of Xu Zhanzhi, Jiang Zhan, and Wang Sengchuo have suffered bitter ruin; their orphaned survivors wander abroad; to speak of the past is grief upon grief."

sentences.zh: 可令歸居本宅，厚加恤賜。

translations.literal: They may be ordered to return and dwell in their original residences, with generous added relief and gifts."
translations.idiomatic: Let them return to their original residences and receive generous relief and gifts."

sentences.zh: 」於是三家長給廩。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three families were long supplied with grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the three families received long-term grain rations.

sentences.zh: 三子：聿之、謙之，為元凶所殺。

translations.literal: Three sons: Yuzhi and Qianzhi were killed by the Prince of Evil Origin.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Yuzhi and Qianzhi were killed by the Prince of Evil Origin.

sentences.zh: 恆之嗣侯，尚太祖第十五女南陽公主，蚤卒，無子。

translations.literal: Hengzhi inherited the marquisate, married Taizu's fifteenth daughter Princess Nanyang, died young, and had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhi inherited the marquisate, married Taizu's fifteenth daughter Princess Nanyang, died young, and left no sons.

sentences.zh: 聿之子孝嗣紹封，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: Yuzhi's son Xiaosi succeeded to the enfeoffment; when Qi received the abdication the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi's son Xiaosi succeeded to the enfeoffment; when Qi received the abdication the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 江湛，字徽淵，濟陽考城人，湘州刺史夷子也。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan, styled Huiyuan, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang, son of Xiangzhou Inspector Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan, styled Huiyuan, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery and was the son of Xiangzhou Inspector Yi.

sentences.zh: 居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: In mourning he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He won renown for filial devotion during mourning.

sentences.zh: 愛好文義，喜彈棋鼓琴，兼明算術。

translations.literal: He loved literary principle, delighted in pitch-pot and the zither, and was also skilled in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He loved letters and moral discourse, delighted in pitch-pot and the zither, and was also skilled in calculation.

sentences.zh: 初為著作佐郎，遷彭城王義康司徒行參軍，南譙王義宣左軍功曹。

translations.literal: He first served as Assistant Gentleman of the Writing Office, then moved to Acting Army Staff Officer to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang as Grand Tutor, and Merit Officer of the Left Army to Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Assistant Gentleman of the Writing Office, then became Acting Army Staff Officer to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang as Grand Tutor and Merit Officer of the Left Army to Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 復為義康司徒主簿，太子中舍人。

translations.literal: He again served as Chief Clerk to Yikang as Grand Tutor and as Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Chief Clerk to Yikang as Grand Tutor and as Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 司空檀道濟為子求湛妹婚，不許。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Tan Daoji sought Zhan's younger sister in marriage for his son; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Tan Daoji sought Zhan's younger sister in marriage for his son; Zhan refused.

sentences.zh: 義康有命，又不從。

translations.literal: Yikang gave an order; again he did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang gave an order; again he did not comply.

sentences.zh: 時人重其立志。

translations.literal: Men of the time respected his firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time respected his firm resolve.

sentences.zh: 義康欲引與日夕，湛固求外出，乃以為武陵內史，還為司徒從事中郎，遷太子中庶子，尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: Yikang wished to keep him day and night; Zhan firmly sought to go outside and was therefore made Interior Administrator of Wuling; he returned as Attendant of the Secretariat Staff, became Senior Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and moved to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang wished to keep him at his side day and night; Zhan firmly sought an outside post and was made Interior Administrator of Wuling; he returned as Attendant of the Secretariat Staff, became Senior Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and moved to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 隨王誕為北中郎將、南徐州刺史，以湛為長史、南東海太守，政事委之。

translations.literal: Prince of Sui Dan was North General of the Household and Governor of Southern Xuzhou; Zhan was made Chief Clerk and Administrator of Southern Donghai, and administration was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Sui Dan was North General of the Household and Governor of Southern Xuzhou, Zhan was made Chief Clerk and Administrator of Southern Donghai, and administration was entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年，徵為侍中，任以機密，領本州大中正，遷左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia he was summoned as Palace Attendant, entrusted with confidential matters, held concurrently as Senior Rectifier of his native commandery, and moved to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia he was summoned as Palace Attendant, entrusted with confidential matters, held concurrently as Senior Rectifier of his native commandery, and became General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 時改選學職，以太尉江夏王義恭領國子祭酒，湛及侍中何攸之領博士。

translations.literal: At that time academic offices were reformed in selection; Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia Yigong held concurrently Rector of the National University, and Zhan with Palace Attendant He Youzhi held concurrently Erudites.
translations.idiomatic: At that time academic offices were reformed; Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia Yigong held concurrently Rector of the National University, and Zhan with Palace Attendant He Youzhi served concurrently as Erudites.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he became Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 家甚貧約，不營財利，餉饋盈門，一無所受，無兼衣餘食。

translations.literal: His household was very poor and spare; he did not pursue wealth, gifts filled his gate yet he accepted none, and he had no spare garments or leftover food.
translations.idiomatic: His household was very poor; he did not pursue wealth, gifts filled his gate yet he accepted none, and he had no spare garments or leftover food.

sentences.zh: 嘗為上所召，值浣衣，稱疾經日，衣成然後赴。

translations.literal: Once when summoned by the emperor he happened to be washing clothes; he pleaded illness for a full day and went only after the clothes were finished.
translations.idiomatic: Once when summoned by the emperor he was washing clothes; he pleaded illness for a full day and went only after the clothes were finished.

sentences.zh: 牛餓，馭人求草，湛良久曰：「可與飲。

translations.literal: An ox was hungry; the driver sought fodder; after a long while Zhan said, "Give it drink."
translations.idiomatic: When an ox was hungry and the driver sought fodder, Zhan said after a long pause, "Give it drink."

sentences.zh: 」在選職，頗有刻核之譏，而公平無私，不受請謁，論者以此稱焉。

translations.literal: In his selection post he drew considerable censure for severity, yet he was fair and without private bias, accepted no solicitations, and critics praised him on this account.
translations.idiomatic: In his selection post he drew censure for severity, yet he was fair and unbiased, accepted no solicitations, and critics praised him on that account.

sentences.zh: 上大舉北代，舉朝為不可，唯湛贊成之。

translations.literal: The emperor launched a great northern campaign; the whole court held it impossible, only Zhan endorsed it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor launched a great northern campaign the whole court opposed it; only Zhan endorsed it.

sentences.zh: 索虜至瓜步，領軍將軍劉遵考率軍出江上，以湛兼領軍，軍事處分，一以委焉。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians reached Guabu; General Who Commands the Army Liu Zunkao led troops out on the river; Zhan was given concurrent command of the army, and all military disposition was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei reached Guabu, General Who Commands the Army Liu Zunkao led troops onto the river; Zhan was given concurrent command of the army, and all military disposition was entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 虜遣使求婚，上召太子劭以下集議，眾並謂宜許，湛曰：「戎狄無信，許之無益。

translations.literal: The barbarians sent envoys to seek marriage; the emperor summoned the Crown Prince Shao and those below to assemble in deliberation; all said it should be granted; Zhan said, "The Rong and Di are faithless—granting it would be of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians sent envoys to seek marriage, the emperor summoned Crown Prince Shao and the court to deliberate; all said it should be granted; Zhan said, "The barbarians are faithless—granting the request would do no good."

sentences.zh: 」劭怒，謂湛曰：「今三王在厄，詎宜苟執異議。

translations.literal: Shao was angry and said to Zhan, "Now the three princes are in peril—how can you stubbornly hold to a dissenting view?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao was angry and said to Zhan, "The three princes are in peril now—how can you stubbornly dissent?"

sentences.zh: 」聲色甚厲。

translations.literal: His voice and expression were very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: His voice and expression were very fierce.

sentences.zh: 坐散俱出，劭使班劍及左右推之，殆將側倒。

translations.literal: When the session broke up and all went out, Shao had his armed attendants and guards push him, nearly tipping him sideways.
translations.idiomatic: When the session ended and all went out, Shao had his armed attendants and guards push him, nearly tipping him over.

sentences.zh: 劭又謂上曰：「北伐敗辱，數州淪破，獨有斬江湛，可以謝天下。

translations.literal: Shao also said to the emperor, "The northern campaign ended in defeat and disgrace, several provinces were lost and broken—only by executing Jiang Zhan can we answer to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Shao also told the emperor, "The northern campaign ended in defeat and disgrace and several provinces were lost—only by executing Jiang Zhan can we answer to the realm."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「北伐自我意，江湛但不異耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The northern campaign was my own idea; Jiang Zhan merely did not dissent—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The northern campaign was my own idea; Jiang Zhan merely did not dissent—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」劭後燕集，未嘗命湛。

translations.literal: Afterward at Shao's banquets Zhan was never invited.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward at Shao's banquets Zhan was never invited.

sentences.zh: 常謂上曰：「江湛佞人，不宜親也。

translations.literal: He often told the emperor, "Jiang Zhan is a flatterer and should not be kept close."
translations.idiomatic: He often told the emperor, "Jiang Zhan is a flatterer and should not be kept close."

sentences.zh: 」上乃為劭長子偉之娉湛第三女，欲以和之。

translations.literal: The emperor then betrothed Shao's eldest son Weizhi to Zhan's third daughter, wishing to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then betrothed Shao's eldest son Weizhi to Zhan's third daughter, hoping to reconcile them.

sentences.zh: 上將廢劭，使湛具詔草。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to depose Shao, he had Zhan draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to depose Shao, he had Zhan draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 劭之入弑也，湛直上省，聞叫噪之聲，乃匿傍小屋中。

translations.literal: When Shao entered to commit regicide, Zhan went straight up to the Secretariat; hearing shouts and uproar, he hid in a small room nearby.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao entered to kill his father, Zhan went straight to the Secretariat; hearing shouts and uproar, he hid in a small room nearby.

sentences.zh: 劭遣收之，舍吏紿云：「不在此。

translations.literal: Shao sent men to seize him; the lodging clerk deceived them, saying, "He is not here."
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent men to seize him; the lodging clerk lied, saying, "He is not here."

sentences.zh: 」兵士即殺舍吏，乃得湛。

translations.literal: The soldiers at once killed the lodging clerk and thus got Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers at once killed the lodging clerk and thus seized Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛據窗受害，意色不撓。

translations.literal: Zhan braced himself at the window as he was struck; his expression did not flinch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan braced himself at the window as he was struck; his expression did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 時年四十六。

translations.literal: He was forty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-six.

sentences.zh: 湛五子恁、恕、憼、愻、法壽，皆見殺。

translations.literal: Zhan's five sons Ren, Shu, Cong, Xun, and Fashou were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's five sons Ren, Shu, Cong, Xun, and Fashou were all killed.

sentences.zh: 初，湛家數見怪異，未敗少日，所眠床忽有數升血。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhan's household had repeatedly seen strange omens; a few days before his fall, several sheng of blood suddenly appeared on the bed where he slept.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhan's household had repeatedly seen strange omens; a few days before his fall, several sheng of blood suddenly appeared on his bed.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，追贈左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，本官如故，諡曰忠簡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he was posthumously made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the ceremonial set of the Three Excellencies and Opening of a Government Office, with the added title Regular Attendant Cavalier, his former offices unchanged, posthumous title Duke Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he was posthumously made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies and Opening of a Government Office, with the added title Regular Attendant Cavalier, his former offices unchanged, and given the posthumous title Duke Zhongjian.

sentences.zh: 長子恁，尚太祖第九女淮陽長公主，為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ren married Taizu's ninth daughter Princess Huaiyang, and served as Assistant Gentleman of the Writing Office.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ren married Taizu's ninth daughter Princess Huaiyang and served as Assistant Gentleman of the Writing Office.

sentences.zh: 王僧綽，琅邪臨沂人，左光祿大夫曇首子也。

translations.literal: Wang Sengchuo, a man of Linyi in Langye, was son of Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Tanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengchuo came from Linyi in Langye commandery and was the son of Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Tanshou.

sentences.zh: 幼有大成之度，弱年眾以國器許之。

translations.literal: As a child he had the measure of great accomplishment; in his youth all acknowledged him as material for the state.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he showed the measure of great accomplishment; in his youth all acknowledged him as a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 好學有理思，練悉朝典。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had principled thought, and was thoroughly versed in court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and thought with principle, and was thoroughly versed in court regulations.

sentences.zh: 年十三，太祖引見，下拜便流涕哽咽，上亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: At thirteen Taizu received him in audience; he bowed and at once wept with choked sobs; the emperor too was overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Taizu received him in audience; he bowed and at once wept with choked sobs, and the emperor too was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 襲封豫章縣侯，尚太祖長女東陽獻公主。

translations.literal: He inherited enfeoffment as Marquis of Yuzhang county and married Taizu's eldest daughter Princess Dongyang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate of Yuzhang county and married Taizu's eldest daughter Princess Dongyang Xian.

sentences.zh: 初為江夏王義恭司徒參軍，轉始興王文學，秘書丞，司徒左長史，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He first served as Army Staff Officer to Prince of Jiangxia Yikang as Grand Tutor, then became Literary Companion to Prince of Shixing, Secretary Director, Left Chief Clerk to the Grand Tutor, and Senior Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Army Staff Officer to Prince of Jiangxia Yikang as Grand Tutor, then became Literary Companion to Prince of Shixing, Secretary Director, Left Chief Clerk to the Grand Tutor, and Senior Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，徙尚書吏部郎，參掌大選。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was moved to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and took part in governing the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he became Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and took part in governing the great selection of officials.

sentences.zh: 究識流品，諳悉人物，拔才舉能，咸得其分。

translations.literal: He thoroughly knew grades of talent, was well acquainted with persons, and in raising the able and promoting talent all received their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: He thoroughly knew grades of talent, was well acquainted with persons, and in promoting the able assigned each to his proper place.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷侍中，任以機密。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to Palace Attendant and entrusted with confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he became Palace Attendant and was entrusted with confidential matters.

sentences.zh: 僧綽沈深有局度，不以才能高人。

translations.literal: Sengchuo was deep and steady and had breadth of vision; he did not set himself above others by talent.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo was deep, steady, and broad in vision; he did not set himself above others by talent.

sentences.zh: 先是，父曇首與王華並為太祖所任，華子嗣人才既劣，位遇亦輕。

translations.literal: Earlier his father Tanshou and Wang Hua were both entrusted by Taizu; Hua's son Si had inferior talent and lighter rank and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his father Tanshou and Wang Hua were both entrusted by Taizu; Hua's son Si had inferior talent and lighter rank and favor.

sentences.zh: 僧綽嘗謂中書侍郎蔡興宗曰：「弟名位應與新建齊，超至今日，蓋由姻戚所致也。

translations.literal: Sengchuo once said to Vice Director of the Secretariat Cai Xingzong, "My younger brother's name and rank ought to stand level with Xinjian; that I have risen above today is surely due to marriage kinship."
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo once told Vice Director of the Secretariat Cai Xingzong, "My younger brother's name and rank ought to stand level with Xinjian; that I have risen above today is surely due to marriage kinship."

sentences.zh: 」新建者，嗣之封也。

translations.literal: Xinjian was Si's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Xinjian was Si's enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 及為侍中，時年二十九。

translations.literal: When he became Palace Attendant he was twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Palace Attendant he was twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚嘗問其年，僧綽自嫌蚤達，逡巡良久乃答，其謙虛自退若此。

translations.literal: Prince of Shixing Jun once asked his age; Sengchuo, self-conscious of early advancement, hesitated a long while before answering—his modest self-restraint was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shixing Jun once asked his age; Sengchuo, self-conscious of having risen early, hesitated a long while before answering—such was his modest self-restraint.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，太祖頗以後事為念，以其年少，方欲大相付託，朝政小大，皆與參焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia Taizu thought much about affairs after his time; because Sengchuo was young, he was just then about to entrust him greatly; matters of court policy large and small were all referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanjia Taizu thought much about affairs after his time; because Sengchuo was young, he was about to entrust him heavily; matters of court policy, large and small, were all referred to him.

sentences.zh: 從兄徽，清介士也，懼其太盛，勸令損抑。

translations.literal: His elder cousin by the paternal line Hui was a man of pure integrity; fearing he had grown too great, he urged him to restrain and reduce himself.
translations.idiomatic: His elder cousin by the paternal line Hui was a man of pure integrity; fearing Sengchuo had grown too great, he urged him to restrain himself.

sentences.zh: 僧綽乃求吳郡及廣州，上並不許。

translations.literal: Sengchuo then sought Wu commandery and Guang province; the emperor granted neither.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo then sought Wu commandery and Guang province; the emperor granted neither.

sentences.zh: 會二凶巫蠱事泄，上獨先召僧綽具言之。

translations.literal: When the witchcraft affair of the two villains leaked out, the emperor first summoned Sengchuo alone and told him the whole matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the witchcraft affair of the two villains leaked out, the emperor first summoned Sengchuo alone and told him everything.

sentences.zh: 及將廢立，使尋求前朝舊典。

translations.literal: When about to depose and establish, he had him search out precedents of former dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: When about to depose one heir and establish another, he had him search out precedents of former dynasties.

sentences.zh: 劭於東宮夜饗將士，僧綽密以啟聞，上又令撰漢魏以來廢諸王故事。

translations.literal: When Shao feasted his officers at night in the Eastern Palace, Sengchuo secretly reported it; the emperor also had him compile stories since Han and Wei of deposing princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao feasted his officers at night in the Eastern Palace, Sengchuo secretly reported it; the emperor also had him compile precedents since Han and Wei for deposing princes.

sentences.zh: 撰畢，送與江湛、徐湛之。

translations.literal: When the compilation was finished it was sent to Jiang Zhan and Xu Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished it was sent to Jiang Zhan and Xu Zhanzhi.

sentences.zh: 湛之欲立隨王誕，江湛欲立南平王鑠，太祖欲立建平王宏，議久不決。

translations.literal: Zhanzhi wished to establish Prince of Sui Dan; Jiang Zhan wished to establish Prince of Nanping Shuo; Taizu wished to establish Prince of Jianping Hong; deliberation long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhi wished to name Prince of Sui Dan heir; Jiang Zhan wished to name Prince of Nanping Shuo; Taizu wished to name Prince of Jianping Hong; deliberation dragged on.

sentences.zh: 延妃即湛之女，鑠妃即湛妹。

translations.literal: Dan's consort was Zhanzhi's daughter; Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's consort was Zhanzhi's daughter; Shuo's consort was Zhanzhi's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂僧綽曰：「諸人各為身計，便無與國家同憂者。

translations.literal: Taizu said to Sengchuo, "Each of these men schemes for himself; there is no one who shares the state's anxiety."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told Sengchuo, "Each of these men schemes for himself; there is no one who shares the state's anxiety."

sentences.zh: 」僧綽曰：「建立之事，仰由聖懷。

translations.literal: Sengchuo said, "The matter of establishment depends on your sacred intent."
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo said, "The matter of establishing an heir depends on your sacred intent."

sentences.zh: 臣謂唯宜速斷，不可稽緩。

translations.literal: I hold that you should decide swiftly and not delay.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that you should decide swiftly and not delay.

sentences.zh: 當斷不斷，反受其亂。

translations.literal: When one should decide and does not, one instead suffers disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When one should decide and does not, one instead suffers disorder.

sentences.zh: 願以義割恩，略小不忍。

translations.literal: I wish you would sever affection by righteousness and set aside small unwillingness to endure.
translations.idiomatic: I wish you would sever affection by righteousness and set aside small unwillingness to endure.

sentences.zh: 不爾，便應坦懷如初，無煩疑論。

translations.literal: If not, you should open your heart as at first and have no need for suspicious debate.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you should open your heart as before and have no need for suspicious debate.

sentences.zh: 淮南云：'以石投水，吳越之善沒取之。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi says: 'Cast a stone into water, and the skilled divers of Wu and Yue will retrieve it.'
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says: "Cast a stone into water, and the skilled divers of Wu and Yue will retrieve it."

sentences.zh: '事機雖密，易致宣廣，不可使難生慮表，取笑千載。

translations.literal: Though the affair is secret, it is easy for it to spread and become widely known; you must not let trouble arise on the surface of deliberation and become a laughingstock for a thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Though the affair is secret, it can easily spread; you must not let trouble show on the surface and become a laughingstock for a thousand years."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿可謂能斷大事。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You may be said able to decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You may truly be said able to decide great affairs.

sentences.zh: 此事重，不可不殷勤三思。

translations.literal: This matter is weighty and cannot but be thrice considered with earnest care.
translations.idiomatic: This matter is weighty and must be considered thrice with earnest care.

sentences.zh: 且庶人始亡，人將謂我無復慈愛之道。

translations.literal: Moreover the commoner has only just perished; men will say I no longer have the way of kindness and love.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the heir has only just been cast down; men will say I no longer have the way of kindness and love.

sentences.zh: 」僧綽曰：「臣恐千載之後，言陛下唯能裁弟，不能裁兒。

translations.literal: Sengchuo said, "I fear that after a thousand years men will say Your Majesty could only judge younger brothers and could not judge sons."
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo said, "I fear that after a thousand years men will say Your Majesty could judge younger brothers but not sons."

sentences.zh: 」上默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 江湛同侍坐，出閣，謂僧綽曰：「卿向言，將不大傷切直。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan had sat in attendance together; leaving the pavilion he said to Sengchuo, "What you just said will wound rather deeply with blunt directness."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan had sat in attendance; leaving the pavilion he told Sengchuo, "What you just said will wound rather deeply with blunt directness."

sentences.zh: 」僧綽曰：「弟亦恨君不直。」

translations.literal: Sengchuo said, "I too regret that you, my younger brother, were not direct."
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo said, "I too regret that you were not direct."

sentences.zh: 及劭弑逆，江湛在尚書上省，聞變，歎曰：「不用僧綽言，以至於此。

translations.literal: When Shao committed regicide, Jiang Zhan was in the upper offices of the Secretariat; hearing the upheaval he sighed and said, "Had we not taken Sengchuo's words, it would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: When Shao committed regicide, Jiang Zhan was in the upper offices of the Secretariat; hearing the upheaval he sighed and said, "Had we taken Sengchuo's advice, it would not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 」劭既立，轉為吏部尚書，委以事任，事在《二凶傳》。

translations.literal: After Shao was established he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and entrusted with affairs; the matter is in the Biography of the Two Villains.
translations.idiomatic: After Shao was established he became Director of the Ministry of Personnel and was entrusted with affairs; the matter is recorded in the Biography of the Two Villains.

sentences.zh: 頃之，劭料檢太祖巾箱及江湛家書疏，得僧綽所啟饗士並廢諸王事，乃收害焉，時年三十一。

translations.literal: Before long Shao examined Taizu's scarf-box and Jiang Zhan's household letters and memorials, found Sengchuo's reports on feasting officers and deposing the princes, and seized and killed him; he was thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shao examined Taizu's scarf-box and Jiang Zhan's household papers, found Sengchuo's reports on feasting officers and deposing the princes, and had him seized and killed; he was thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 因此陷北第諸王侯，以為與僧綽有異志，並殺僧綽門客太學博士賈匪之、奉朝請司馬文穎、建平國常侍司馬仲秀等。

translations.literal: On this account he implicated the princes and marquises of the Northern Residence, holding that they shared Sengchuo's divergent intent, and jointly killed Sengchuo's clients Erudite of the National University Jia Feizhi, Court Attendant Sima Wenying, Regular Attendant of the Principality of Jianping Sima Zhongxiu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: On this account he implicated the princes and marquises of the Northern Residence, holding that they shared Sengchuo's divergent intent, and also killed Sengchuo's clients Erudite Jia Feizhi, Court Attendant Sima Wenying, Regular Attendant Sima Zhongxiu, and others.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，追贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，諡曰湣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he was posthumously made Regular Attendant Cavalier and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, posthumous title Marquis Min.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he was posthumously made Regular Attendant Cavalier and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, with the posthumous title Marquis Min.

sentences.zh: 初，太社西空地一區，吳時丁奉宅，孫晧流徙其家。

translations.literal: Earlier, a vacant plot west of the Grand Altar of Earth had been Ding Feng's residence in Wu times; Sun Hao exiled his household from it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a vacant plot west of the Grand Altar of Earth had been Ding Feng's residence in Wu times; Sun Hao exiled his household from it.

sentences.zh: 江左初為周顗、蘇峻宅，其後為袁悅宅，又為章武王司馬秀宅，皆以凶終。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Jin it first served Zhou Yi and Su Jun; later it was Yuan Yue's residence, then Prince of Zhangwu Sima Xiu's—all ended in violent death.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Jin it first served Zhou Yi and Su Jun; later it was Yuan Yue's residence, then Prince of Zhangwu Sima Xiu's—all ended in violent death.

sentences.zh: 後給臧燾，亦頗遇喪禍，故世稱為凶地。

translations.literal: Later it was given to Zang Can, who also met considerable mourning calamity; the age therefore called it an ill-omened place.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was given to Zang Can, who also met considerable mourning calamity; the age therefore called it an ill-omened place.

sentences.zh: 僧綽常以正達自居，謂宅無吉凶，請以為第。

translations.literal: Sengchuo often set himself up as upright and penetrating, held that dwellings have no good or ill fortune, and asked to take it as his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo often set himself up as upright and penetrating, held that dwellings have no good or ill fortune, and asked to take it as his residence.

sentences.zh: 始就造築，未及居而敗。

translations.literal: He had just begun construction and, before he could dwell there, met ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He had just begun construction and, before he could move in, met ruin.

sentences.zh: 子儉嗣，升明末，為齊國尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: His son Jian inherited; at the end of the Shengming era he served as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat in the State of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian inherited; at the end of the Shengming era he served as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat in the State of Qi.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：甚矣，宋氏之家難也，仇釁所鐘，親地兼極，雖復傾天滅道，跡非嫌路，而災隙內兆，邪蠱外興，天性既離，愛敬同盡，探雀請熊，非無前釁，猜防之道，有未足乎。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: How severe were the household calamities of the Song! Enmity and grievance converged, kinship and territory both reached their extreme; though heaven was overturned and the Way extinguished, the traces were not on a path of suspicion alone—yet disaster fissures sprouted within, wicked witchcraft rose without, natural affection was already sundered and love and respect alike exhausted; seeking the sparrow and inviting the bear—there were not lacking prior provocations; were the ways of suspicion and guard not yet sufficient?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: How severe were the Song household calamities! Enmity and grievance converged, kinship and territory both reached their extreme; though heaven was overturned and the Way extinguished, the traces were not on a path of suspicion alone—yet disaster fissures sprouted within, wicked witchcraft rose without, natural affection was sundered and love and respect alike exhausted; seeking the sparrow and inviting the bear—there were prior provocations; were the ways of suspicion and guard not yet sufficient?

sentences.zh: 世祖弱年輕躁，夙無朝寵，累任邊外，未嘗居中。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu in his youth was light and rash, long without court favor, repeatedly posted to the outer borders, never stationed in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu in his youth was light and rash, long without court favor, repeatedly posted to the outer borders, never stationed in the center.

sentences.zh: 當璧之重，將由愛立，臣主回疑，事無蚤斷。

translations.literal: The weight of holding the jade disk was to be established through affection; lord and minister turned in doubt, and the affair had no early decision.
translations.idiomatic: The weight of holding the jade disk was to be settled through affection; lord and minister turned in doubt, and the affair had no early decision.

sentences.zh: 若使守器以長，命不待賢，則密禍自銷，危機可免。

translations.literal: If one had kept the vessel by seniority and fate had not awaited the worthy, secret calamity would have extinguished itself and crisis could have been avoided.
translations.idiomatic: If the heir had been kept by seniority and fate had not awaited the worthy, secret calamity would have extinguished itself and crisis could have been avoided.

sentences.zh: 聖哲之訓，豈欺我哉！

translations.literal: The teaching of the sage and wise—would it deceive us?
translations.idiomatic: The teaching of the sage and wise—would it deceive us?

sentences.zh: 昔山濤舉羊祜為太子太傅，蓋欲以後事委之，而羊公短世。

translations.literal: Formerly Shan Tao recommended Yang Hu as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, intending to entrust later affairs to him, but Lord Yang died young.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Shan Tao recommended Yang Hu as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, intending to entrust later affairs to him, but Yang Hu died young.

sentences.zh: 僧綽綢繆主心，將任以國重，而宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: Sengchuo bound close to the ruler's heart and was about to be entrusted with the weight of the state, but the imperial carriage halted at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo bound close to the ruler's heart and was about to be entrusted with the weight of the state, but the emperor died before he could take office.

sentences.zh: 二臣並以道德謙沖，名高兩代。

translations.literal: Both ministers were alike for moral virtue and modest restraint, their names lofty across two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Both ministers were alike for moral virtue and modest restraint, their names lofty across two generations.

sentences.zh: 胙未中年，功謝成日，惜矣哉！

translations.literal: Their blessings had not reached mid-years; their merit faded before completion—how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Their blessings had not reached mid-years; their merit faded before completion—how regrettable!
